You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From c0e310188299358279fc27c88512f94db78991a6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Date: Thu, 27 Feb 2020 08:57:04 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915: Skip barriers inside waits

Attaching to the i915_active barrier is a two stage process, and a flush
is only effective when the barrier is activation. Thus it is possible
for us to see a barrier, and attempt to flush, only for our flush to
have no effect. As such, before attempting to activate signaling on the
fence we need to double check it is a fence!

Fixes: d13a31770077 ("drm/i915: Flush idle barriers when waiting")
Closes: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/intel/issues/1333
Signed-off-by: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Cc: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Andi Shyti <andi.shyti@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20200227085723.1961649-1-chris@chris-wilson.co.uk
---
 drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c | 3 +++
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+)

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c
index 0b12d5023800..7b3d6c12ad61 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c
@@ -453,6 +453,9 @@ static void enable_signaling(struct i915_active_fence *active)
 {
 	struct dma_fence *fence;
 
+	if (unlikely(is_barrier(active)))
+		return;
+
 	fence = i915_active_fence_get(active);
 	if (!fence)
 		return;
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the attempt to flush a barrier that was not yet activated, leading to ineffective flush operations. The code did not properly check if the active fence was indeed a fence and not a barrier before proceeding with the flush, which could result in unexpected behavior or failures in the signaling process. The patch adds a check to skip the flush operation if the active fence is identified as a barrier.

    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the attempt to flush a barrier that was not yet activated, leading to ineffective flush operations. The code did not properly check if the active fence was indeed a fence and not a barrier before proceeding with the flush, which could result in unexpected behavior or failures in the signaling process. The patch adds a check to skip the flush operation if the active fence is identified as a barrier.
